features.title: Start with a question
features.body: Name the CASEBOOK for the investigation you are working on. The board shares the existing local casebook, so pins and analyst notes remain available in the other research views.

features.title: Find and place evidence
features.body: Choose Pin a record, search a name, institution or question, and press Search. Results include records, identities and relationships. Pin record adds an existing item with its original source references; Show 30 more expands the search. Up to 250 pins can be kept.

features.title: Read the source beside the claim
features.body: Open a pin to inspect its evidence tier, recorded status, date basis, amounts, responses, competing explanations, geography and source ledger. Your analyst note stays separate. Remove this pin removes the saved reference, never the underlying source record.

features.title: Arrange the material your way
features.body: Drag a pin by its grip, or focus the grip and use arrow keys; Shift moves farther. The inspector also has Move pin buttons. Pin positions organize your research and are not geographic locations.

features.title: Connect pins with a testable question
features.body: After pinning at least two items, choose Connect pins. Select From, To and Purpose: Question, Compare, Counter-evidence to check or Follow-up. Write what you would check, then Add thread. A wool thread is your analytical annotation, not a verified relationship.

features.title: Distinguish sourced links from your threads
features.body: The Sourced links between pinned identities checkbox shows existing documentary relationships where both endpoints are pinned. The connection ledger labels these separately from Analyst threads. Inspect sources opens the original edge; Remove thread removes only your annotation.

features.title: Choose a comfortable reading view
features.body: Board lays out the pins; List shows every pin in reading order. Arrange resets positions while keeping threads and notes. Depth changes presentation only. The canvas initially shows 60 pins and Show 60 more expands it; List contains every saved pin.

features.title: Write down what would change your mind
features.body: Use the question-closing field to name the evidence that would resolve or disprove your idea. Notes & exports opens the full Casebook: question, falsifier, per-record notes, saved views, JSON export and reading-brief export. These notes are user-entered research.

features.title: Keep a portable backup
features.body: Export downloads the pins, source references, analyst notes and board layout. Restore reads a supported JSON backup and merges it while retaining existing pins, notes, question and positions. Local browser storage is not a cloud backup; export before clearing it.

features.title: Keep the wider work available
features.body: Explore the atlas opens geographic investigation. The navigation keeps every specialist register, source ledger and saved research view available. Public assets & finance contains the separate, source-bound Fairfax / IDBI exercise.

features.title: Choose a starting point
features.body: The overview links to the shared investigation workspace, education, water and food, public works and the corporate record.

features.title: Open the full register
features.body: Use a section link to open its specialist page. Shared workspace filters may narrow what you see; the dossier view exposes the original page.

features.title: Read the scope
features.body: Each collection is a dated, partial register. A count describes the retained dataset, not all activity in India.

features.title: Search by a known identifier
features.body: Enter at least two characters of a company, ticker, ISIN, minister, group, state or alias. Search matches literal text.

features.title: Choose the right kind of result
features.body: Results are grouped into companies, ministers, conglomerates, states and graph entities. Follow the relevant result to its profile.

features.title: Keep identities separate
features.body: A similar name is not a verified identity match. Check identifiers and source context before treating two records as the same person or company.

features.title: Choose what the color means
features.body: Switch between listed market cap, listed-company count, public-sector share, state GSDP and sector concentration. Read each metric’s definition.

features.title: Narrow the comparison
features.body: Use exchange, index, sector, scale and marker controls to compare a defined population. Select a state to inspect it.

features.title: Use the underlying records
features.body: Open a state or company from the map and table. Headquarters and registration geography do not establish where money was spent.

features.title: Read the selected state
features.body: The profile brings together the listed companies, industrial structure and political representation retained for this state.

features.title: Open a company or related register
features.body: Follow linked company names and related research sections to inspect the underlying record.

features.title: Keep the denominator
features.body: State totals describe the included companies and dated data. Missing records and headquarters concentration do not prove local economic impact.

features.title: Confirm the company
features.body: Check its name, ticker or ISIN and profile sources before following its group and sector links.

features.title: Track a company locally
features.body: Use “+ track” to add this company to the Watchlist. The tracked button removes it. This is local to this browser; it does not subscribe you to live alerts.

features.title: Inspect the dated record
features.body: Read source dates, ownership, location and the linked relationships. A recorded snapshot does not guarantee the same position today.

features.title: Choose a layer
features.body: Everything combines the case-study and national layers. Case study, Political and Capital narrow the graph.

features.title: Inspect an actual edge
features.body: Use graph filters for evidence tier, family and relationship type. Table view offers the same retained data without relying on the visualization.

features.title: Check a path against its baseline
features.body: Enter names in the Path finder. A short path or high-degree hub reflects graph structure; it does not establish coordination.

features.title: Choose geography and a layer
features.body: Use mode and layer controls, entity search and year boundaries to narrow this network. Unknown dates and placements keep their stated limits.

features.title: Explore a neighborhood
features.body: Select an entity, set Focus hops, pin or unpin it and inspect a relationship. Clear focus returns to the wider network.

features.title: Use the readable alternative
features.body: Show table view to read the edges, copy the link to preserve this view or reset the filters. Spatial proximity is not an evidence link.

features.title: Filter the dated roster
features.body: Choose a minister rank. Select a state on the representation map and use clear to remove the state focus.

features.title: Read portfolio and sources
features.body: The roster records ministers, ministries and regulatory reach. Party composition and changes are tied to the dataset’s as-of date.

features.title: Distinguish authority from conduct
features.body: Holding a portfolio or chairing an institution does not establish a personal decision, attendance, vote or wrongdoing.

features.title: Choose scope and view
features.body: Use Scope for centre, states or both, then View for ledger, map or graph. Search by winner, project or awarding body.

features.title: Inspect disclosure before concentration
features.body: Read bidder-count and value coverage. A missing bidder count is unknown competition, not a single-bid award.

features.title: Open the national procurement trail
features.body: The linked CPPP section has its own filters and provenance. A tender notice, award and payment are different stages; repeated notices need identity and date checks.

features.title: Find a resource record
features.body: Filter by block, winner or basin. Compare the available allocation and resource registers.

features.title: Read the allocation terms
features.body: Open linked companies and source citations. Preserve resource type, award mechanism, date and recorded amount basis.

features.title: Stop at the source boundary
features.body: A resource award does not by itself establish extraction, revenue received, market power or improper influence.

features.title: Compare the recorded groups
features.body: Choose a group and compare its listed entities, sectors and recorded market cap.

features.title: Inspect footprint and deep dive
features.body: The footprint selector changes the group shown on the map. Open a group for its entity, contract, capital and flow records.

features.title: Keep coverage explicit
features.body: A group with no deep entity map is a research gap. Map positions and aggregate size are not findings about conduct.

features.title: Choose a record family
features.body: Switch between entities, contracts, capital and flows. The ownership tree, maps and tables link back to the same dated records.

features.title: Inspect legal identity
features.body: Read registry identifiers, parent relationships, ownership measures and source citations. Intermediate holding layers may remain unresolved.

features.title: Recognize a coverage gap
features.body: Groups without a built deep dataset show a comparative summary and a visible gap. The former Adani and Reliance page modules are superseded by this shared route.

features.title: Read the case-study network
features.body: Inspect the sourced, tiered entities and relationships. The atlas is a bounded case-study graph.

features.title: Expand a motif
features.body: Open a motif row to see its note, census and evidence limits. Read the integrity check when shown.

features.title: Treat a pattern as a test
features.body: A motif is an arrangement in the retained graph. Its existence does not establish secret coordination or a new allegation.

features.title: Read the reasoning checks
features.body: This reading guide covers base rates, large-network coincidences and the consequences of trying many possible tests.

features.title: Expand a trap
features.body: Open a row under “The ten traps” for the corrective and how the app applies it. The expanded state is reversible.

features.title: Use the checklist
features.body: Run the final checklist before publishing a network-derived claim. Historical adjudicated examples do not transfer a verdict to a new case.

features.title: Read the evidence tiers
features.body: Compare each tier’s requirements, limitations and the claims assigned to it.

features.title: Follow the supporting record
features.body: Use the citations and linked cases to inspect the actual source rather than relying on a colored badge.

features.title: Keep a claim bounded
features.body: A documented source may establish that a statement was made without proving the underlying allegation.

features.title: Start with the comparison population
features.body: Read the denominator and date before evaluating an overlap, donation or contract concentration.

features.title: Inspect the tender ledger
features.body: Follow the source-backed entries and portfolio timing. The ledger marks timing without turning it into personal responsibility.

features.title: Ask what evidence would discriminate
features.body: The final open tests distinguish ordinary large-network overlap from relationships that would carry additional information.

features.title: Set the role threshold
features.body: Choose the minimum recorded roles to narrow the office-holder list. Counts remain tied to the included groups.

features.title: Inspect cross-group roles
features.body: Read the recorded roles and their sources. A common name needs an identity basis before records can be combined.

features.title: Use the false-positive example
features.body: The surname-coincidence section demonstrates why shared surnames are not family, political or business links.

features.title: Choose the graph scope
features.body: Switch between the atlas and control scope before interpreting the template counts.

features.title: Expand a template
features.body: A template reveals its pattern, null-model comparison, ordinary explanation and kill condition.

features.title: Check the symmetry test
features.body: Some graphs are too small or too star-shaped to test. “Untestable” is a limitation, not a negative result.

features.title: Read a candidate mechanism
features.body: Each candidate identifies the structure or record worth investigating and what the current data can support.

features.title: Follow the evidence and next test
features.body: Use the supporting links and proposed checks to move from a candidate to a testable question.

features.title: Keep prioritization separate from proof
features.body: A promising research lead is neither a verified finding nor a probability of wrongdoing.

features.title: Read established and unestablished side by side
features.body: Each assembled item states both what the retained records establish and what they do not.

features.title: Follow a source or linked dossier
features.body: Open the relevant evidence rather than treating the desk’s summary as a new independent source.

features.title: Choose the next record
features.body: The workflow and next steps prioritize missing identifiers, bidder coverage and other records that unblock a check.

features.title: Compare mechanisms with traces
features.body: Each pathway begins with a possible mechanism, the documentary trace it would leave and the observed record.

features.title: Filter by verdict
features.body: Use All or a verdict category to inspect the matching pathways. Empty categories are disabled.

features.title: Read the limits
features.body: Verdicts apply to the stated test and data. They do not establish a person’s hidden motives or make an allegation true by association.

features.title: Read the base rate first
features.body: The opening counts explain how often winners recur across the four included registers.

features.title: Set the overlap threshold
features.body: Change the minimum number of registers to narrow the graph. The winner-list toggle expands or reduces the visible list.

features.title: Check identifiers and sources
features.body: A winner label without a verified legal identifier may not support a cross-register identity join. Repeated wins alone do not establish misconduct.

features.title: Read the account coverage
features.body: Compare published statement years, audit lag, completeness and the dated review boundary.

features.title: Inspect accounts and citations
features.body: Read each amount’s year, accounting label and source. Follow the ledger for the underlying statements.

features.title: Keep receipts and spending separate
features.body: Missing detail is a disclosure gap. Do not add overlapping accounting entries or infer a recipient without a traced record.

features.title: Find an entity or claim
features.body: Search entities, claims and source titles. Active filters are visible and can be cleared.

features.title: Inspect the power map
features.body: Choose a graph node or relation and read its typed, sourced context. Reset graph filters if a prior selection hides results.

features.title: Read what is missing
features.body: Open “What the record does not contain” and Sources. Power-sector proximity or ownership is not a payment trail.

features.title: Find a scheme
features.body: Search by scheme, alias or person, then narrow category, evidence tier, party, metric, level and year.
features.selector: [aria-label="Search schemes by name, alias or person"]

features.title: Choose the comparison view
features.body: Use View and Metric to compare like quantities. Preserve units, periods and administrative levels.

features.title: Read the missing record
features.body: The final coverage section states what was not retained. A budget, allocation, disbursement and benefit received cannot be treated as the same number.

features.title: Choose a finance lens
features.body: Move among the loan, capital and association registers. Search by name, alias, project or place.

features.title: Inspect a record and connections
features.body: Open record reveals the selected entry; Show connections displays its retained relationships. Lender and holder actions narrow the corresponding lens.

features.title: Switch to tables or share the view
features.body: Table view provides a readable alternative. Copy link preserves URL filters. An association or capital holding is not itself a paid loan.

features.title: Read the programme and spending scope
features.body: Compare the retained security-spending records at their stated year, jurisdiction and accounting stage.

features.title: Follow the contract or source
features.body: Use the linked records and citations to verify the named buyer, supplier and purpose.

features.title: Preserve the evidence boundary
features.body: An announcement or procurement amount is not proof of delivery, operational use or a completed payment.

features.title: Choose place and funding scope
features.body: Filter state, locality, topic, funding channel, management type and institution level; submit Search. Reset filters restores the full retained register.

features.title: Move between evidence sections
features.body: Jump to Documents & news, Funding routes, Questions to investigate or School counts. Show more expands the relevant list.

features.title: Save or export the working view
features.body: Save a source locally, show Saved only, Copy link or Export CSV. Exports retain source context; they are not a complete census.

features.title: Compare like school counts
features.body: Read management, geography, period and coverage notes. Counts and population change alone do not establish why a school closed.

features.title: Choose place and subject
features.body: Search by place and topic, select a subject lens and food-chain stage, then read the filtered source list.

features.title: Follow the dated sections
features.body: Move among sources, observations, research leads and public tools. Expand records or use their original-source links.

features.title: Keep event and validity dates
features.body: Weather and hazard bulletins are historical records, not live conditions. Food-chain stages organize evidence; they do not trace a shipment by themselves.

features.title: Set the sector and location
features.body: Choose a sector lens, place and search terms to narrow the public-works evidence.

features.title: Inspect stages and comparisons
features.body: The procurement stages, repeat-work checks, rules and source sections keep notices, contracts, delivery and payments separate.

features.title: Compare records carefully
features.body: A repeated contractor or similar notice does not establish repeat physical work. Compare identity, location, scope and date before making that claim.

features.title: Read the correction first
features.body: The opening correction states which earlier claims did not survive review. Later sections use the revised basis.

features.title: Compare distributions and jurisdictions
features.body: Read bidder-count distributions, value comparisons and the two-state comparison with their denominators.

features.title: Check provenance and gaps
features.body: Inspect file provenance, byte counts, digests and missing fields. This selected coverage is not a national competition rate.

features.title: Trace a claim to its source
features.body: The ledger records source identity, access depth and the boundaries of retained evidence.

features.title: Inspect original material
features.body: Follow the source link and locator. A source URL, search snippet and an actually inspected original have different evidentiary strength.

features.title: Check independence
features.body: Repeated references to the same source family are not independent corroboration. A retrieval failure does not establish concealment.

features.title: Read the four invariants
features.body: The methodology explains evidence tiers, the data pipeline, bounded research roles and the app’s refusals.

features.title: Check live integrity
features.body: The integrity section runs against the merged graph on page load. A passed structural check does not verify every source assertion.

features.title: Keep the snapshot date
features.body: Use Data as-of dates before describing a figure as current. The app is a dated research collection, not a live feed.

features.title: Select a sector
features.body: Use a sector button or an All sectors row to change the companies being compared.

features.title: Inspect the company table and map
features.body: Compare recorded market cap, listed-firm HHI, the largest firm’s share and registration locations. Open a company for its sources.

features.title: Keep market boundaries clear
features.body: HHI here concerns included listed firms and recorded market cap. It is not a comprehensive product-market competition finding.

features.title: Read the donation register
features.body: Inspect the recorded donor, recipient, amount, period and disclosure source.

features.title: Follow linked entities and sources
features.body: Use the available group or company links to check identities and the source trail.

features.title: Do not infer a quid pro quo
features.body: A disclosed donation establishes that dated political contribution. A contract, decision or personal benefit requires its own evidence.

features.title: Inspect ownership before ratings
features.body: Compare owner groups, cross-media holdings and the outlet register. Each proportion states its denominator.

features.title: Read outlet-level sources
features.body: Follow owner and source links. Any lean rating is tied to the named rater and date, not asserted as an objective property.

features.title: Read rejected sources and gaps
features.body: The page explains why a single ideological bar would overstate the evidence. Ownership does not establish editorial instruction.

features.title: Review tracked companies
features.body: Companies added with “+ track” on their profile appear here. Open a company to return to its details.

features.title: Manage your local research
features.body: Use the available remove or untrack controls for a tracked company. The page also shows open research questions.

features.title: Know where it is saved
features.body: This watchlist uses this browser’s local storage. It is not a cloud backup, live monitoring subscription or automatic notification service.

features.title: Set the investigation scope
features.body: Use the shared dossier filters to choose the records in this view.

features.title: Switch between Network and Source ledger
features.body: Inspect connections visually or open a record from the readable ledger. Both refer to the retained dossier data.

features.title: Read claim, status and response
features.body: An allegation, response, legal development and adjudicated finding remain different record types. Graph layout does not rank culpability.

features.title: Choose the research scope
features.body: Filter by dossier or show all dossiers. Saved on this device narrows the view to locally saved leads.

features.title: Save a question to revisit
features.body: Use the lead’s save control to toggle its local saved state. It does not send or publish the question.

features.title: Read all four checks
features.body: For every hypothesis, read what would fit, rival explanations, what would defeat it and which records to obtain.

features.title: Choose an institutional role
features.body: Select a role and case, then set the assumptions in the worksheet.

features.title: Test assumptions, not hidden intent
features.body: Compare lawful strategy and an abuse hypothesis. Reset assumptions returns to the supplied defaults.

features.title: Preserve a test plan
features.body: Capture plan revision records the current worksheet; Export scenario JSON keeps revisions and evidence. A scenario outcome is not a forecast or a finding of motive.

features.title: Search the relation ledger
features.body: Filter recorded text by sector, status, relation or endpoint. Previous and Next page through the retained relations.

features.title: Inspect an exact connection or path
features.body: Open a relation in the evidence inspector, or choose Path start, Path destination and Traversal. Reading an edge backward does not reverse a payment.

features.title: Use disconfirming tests
features.body: Review limits, alternatives, responses, research coverage and method examples. Historical findings suggest tests; their accusations do not transfer to another case.

features.title: Find a case or entity
features.body: Search retained evidence or NSE securities. Choose a casefile from the map or index.

features.title: Follow one documented step
features.body: Select a relation in the case network, inspect the source, response and limits, then return to the selected evidence or case.

features.title: Keep the case and evidence
features.body: Save a case or selected evidence to the local Casebook, copy Share view or download Evidence JSON.

features.title: Stop at missing steps
features.body: Read other explanations and the next document to seek. Ownership, context and a traced payment are distinct edges.

features.title: Select a reviewed trail
features.body: Choose the investigation, view and graph scope. The retained trail is bounded by its stated place and time.

features.title: Read payer, payee and stage
features.body: Inspect each documentary hop, amount, instrument and source. A missing transaction path is visibly left open.

features.title: Export and challenge
features.body: Export the complete evidence packet; read rival explanations and what would change the conclusion. Context links do not complete a missing cash path.

features.title: Choose a place and research scope
features.body: Search contracts, institutions or records; narrow city, sector, state, publication window and evidence status.

features.title: Inspect a question on the map
features.body: Zoom, reset or choose a matching case, then inspect the exact source location and source-linked relationship graph.

features.title: Read challenges and chronology
features.body: Compare what the records say with counter-evidence and dated developments. Acquisition gaps remain visible.

features.title: Export the research packet
features.body: The packet preserves the selected evidence and limits. Testable future outcomes are open questions, not validated predictive accuracy.

features.title: Choose a lab section
features.body: Use Model lab sections, filter saved questions and open a retained question or finding.

features.title: Inspect retrieved evidence
features.body: Switch visualization or graph depth. The evidence reader shows source location, identity basis, financial stage and response.

features.title: Read the evaluation before the score
features.body: Saved final evaluation, promotion decision and reproducible training show the actual measured scope. Retrieval relevance is not truth.

features.title: Track observations separately
features.body: Search World Bank projects and read the observation register. Resolution is an observed outcome, not proof that an earlier model predicted it.

features.title: Find a research file
features.body: Choose track, evidence status or search terms, then select a file. Map and Network organize the same retained case.

features.title: Read each relationship stage
features.body: Inspect what the record supports, its stopping point, competing explanations and the institutional decision analysis.

features.title: Search across the wider corpus
features.body: The research sections include fixed cross-sector questions, source candidates, path demonstrations and an identity review queue. Lexical scores are not proof.

features.title: Export or continue the research
features.body: Export research packet preserves the case. The next-record backlog identifies acquisition work; repeated labels remain separate until identity is verified.

features.title: Choose a hypothesis file
features.body: Filter by research theme, current assessment or query; select the case and use Map or Network.

features.title: Separate proposition from record
features.body: Compare what is established, what remains unestablished, rival explanations, rules, powers and chronology.

features.title: Inspect and export
features.body: Open a source reader for its exact locator and limits, or Export research packet. Missing connections remain research questions, never invented factual edges.

features.title: Choose the evidence scope
features.body: Search a company, case or connection, then use Filters for category, place and sector. Map and Network offer two views.

features.title: Inspect the record and response
features.body: Open Show index or a map entry to read the selected claim, finding or outcome and the procedural response.

features.title: Explore city spending context
features.body: Delhi and Mumbai views include Budgets & contracts. These financial context records do not by themselves support a specific allegation.

features.title: Export with limitations
features.body: Export evidence retains claims and responses. Review geographic precision, legal status and what the map can establish before drawing a conclusion.

features.title: Choose the workspace or dossier
features.body: The international finance workspace offers the shared place, layer, date and evidence-tier filters. Open Dossier for its retained record list.

features.title: Read and save a record
features.body: Inspect the record’s type, date, sources and evidence limits. Save to casebook keeps a local research reference; Show 24 more records expands the list.

features.title: Keep the stage and coverage
features.body: This is a partial source-backed register. An announcement, allegation, official response, commitment and completed payment or legal finding must keep their own status.

features.title: Search a defined collection
features.body: Search an event, institution, place or record; narrow Collection, Country and City. More filters reveals year, evidence, status, sector and undated records.

features.title: Choose a readable view
features.body: Globe and Flat map show supplied locations. Network shows retained relationships around a chosen Focus entity. Table provides the full readable record list.

features.title: Inspect the provenance

features.body: Research gaps, Country coverage and Reading the graph distinguish unresearched places from negative findings. A political contribution does not establish an election contract.

steps.title: A reported case, ready to examine
steps.body: This exercise uses the already-reported Fairfax / IDBI strategic-sale case, IN-IDBI-2022. It teaches how to read the existing record; it does not present a new discovery. Status is the retained 14 October 2026 snapshot, researched 15 October. Later developments need separate evidence.
steps.tryLabel: Find IDBI in the finance register

steps.title: Approval is not a completed sale
steps.body: The retained case records the selected-buyer approval on 14 October 2026. Fairfax’s announcement says “no binding definitive agreements”. The record therefore remains at bidding / approved-buyer stage; it does not establish title transfer or proceeds received.
steps.question: Which record would establish a completed sale?
answers: An executed closing / transfer record with conditions met
A line linking the buyer and bank
steps.explanation: A closing or transfer record is needed. Approval and a graph edge preserve their own narrower stage.

steps.title: Separate the sellers and the price
steps.body: The approved scope is 60.72%: Government of India 30.48% and LIC 30.24%. The retained consideration is INR 52,878.0806181 crore for that combined stake. It is not all central-government revenue and is not a verified cash receipt.
steps.question: Can this whole amount be called government cash received?
answers: Yes, because a buyer was approved
No; it covers both sellers and receipts are not established
steps.explanation: Both scope and stage matter: the price covers GoI and LIC, and approval does not establish receipts.

steps.title: Voting power has its own denominator
steps.body: The 6 March 2026 Fairfax proxy records Sixty Two’s voting rights at 41.9% and Watsa’s aggregate owned or controlled voting rights at 43.3%. The aggregate includes Sixty Two and personal holdings. Do not add these percentages or convert them into economic equity or a personal IDBI holding.
steps.question: What do these percentages describe?
answers: A dated voting-rights snapshot at Fairfax
Watsa’s personal economic stake in IDBI
steps.explanation: They are overlapping voting measures in a dated Fairfax proxy, not an IDBI ownership calculation.

steps.title: A funding plan is not a drawdown
steps.body: Fairfax described expected cash, existing credit and potential asset sales. The record supplies no named acquisition lender, committed facility amount or drawdown. Proposed Digit and IIFL Capital contributions are separate proposed transactions, not completed IDBI assets or purchase-price payments.
steps.question: What does the retained funding paragraph establish?
answers: A specific bank paid the purchase price
The proposed contributions are already completed
steps.explanation: The paragraph describes a plan. Commitment documents, named lenders and drawn amounts would be needed for a financed cash path.

steps.title: Test the changed valuation comparator
steps.body: The government-reported figures are INR 94.42 per share for the initial reserve, INR 75.99 for the later benchmark and INR 81 for the winning bid. A changed comparator is already reported; the dataset has not independently reproduced fair value. Obtain full valuation reports, comparable-bank choices, adjustments and the authority and timing of the revision before deciding whether the price was too low.
steps.question: What is the defensible next step?
answers: Label the change proof of corruption
Compare the actual valuation methods and competing explanations
Infer a hidden lender from shared ownership
steps.explanation: The test needs the underlying valuation methods and records. The public figures alone do not establish undervaluation or motive.

steps.title: Keep the question open and testable
steps.body: A bounded conclusion: a strategic buyer was approved in the retained snapshot, while agreements, closing, receipts, acquisition finance and an independently replicated valuation remain unestablished. Your next task is to obtain the missing records, preserve contrary evidence and update the status only when the source supports it.
